review: Bounded closure of extraction security findings

snapshot.result: all manifest file sizes and SHA-256 hashes matched

scope: Only the four findings in the parent report were closed against the immutable review-02 snapshot. Source, snapshots, MC, personal Chrome, live downloads, and registry were not modified or accessed. No helper or test was run by this reviewer.

findings.summary: Worker admission now has cross-process coordination and a hard cap of four live queued/extracting workers.

evidence.detail: MAX_WORKERS is four; queue wait is capped at two hours.
active_worker_count counts live queued/extracting jobs; malformed job JSON conservatively consumes capacity and filesystem errors fail admission.
Existing job IDs return before admission; dispatch.lock serializes counting through the queued-state transition, and rejected new jobs return worker-capacity before writing job state.
worker-capacity leaves the same job ID pending so synchronization can retry after capacity becomes available.
Isolated integration case fills admission slots and asserts rejection creates no orphan job JSON.
Unit coverage counts live waiters and fails closed when a job record is malformed.

verification.tests: Parent-reported pass in artifacts/extraction-native/security-fixes.json; the reviewer read the report and source/test definitions but did not rerun them.
verification.remaining: Malformed records intentionally fail closed and can consume slots until repaired; this prevents cap bypass but may require manual state recovery if four records become corrupt.

findings.recommendation: Keep the cap and stable-ID retry behavior. Consider a documented/manual recovery path for permanently malformed job records.

findings.summary: Listing, test, and extraction subprocesses now have deadlines; timeout terminates and reaps the child, with Windows Job Object cleanup for descendants.

evidence.detail: Each engine operation has a 30-minute deadline.
Windows child processes are assigned to a kill-on-close Job Object; the non-Windows test implementation is a no-op.
wait_child polls to deadline, terminates the job and child, and waits to reap it.
Archive test and extraction route through the deadline-enforcing wait.
Listing uses a bounded reader thread while the parent polls the child exit/deadline, then joins/reaps on failure paths.
Windows unit test uses a 100 ms deadline and asserts timeout plus process reaping.

verification.snapshotCodeReview: verified all three operation paths use timeout handling
verification.tests: Parent-reported 10/10 Rust tests and actual Windows timeout kill/reap test pass in artifacts/extraction-native/security-fixes.json; no 30-minute soak was run.
verification.remaining: The bound is per subprocess, so list + test + extract can take up to roughly 90 minutes, plus at most two hours queued. This is finite but intentionally generous for large archives.

findings.recommendation: No blocking fix remains for the reported unbounded-child issue. Revisit the 30-minute limits if product latency requirements call for a shorter bound.

findings.summary: Completed and superseded secrets are cleaned durably, but a failed extraction retains its current DPAPI secret for explicit retry and uninstall intentionally leaves residual encrypted helper state.

evidence.detail: Deletion IDs are persisted, deleted through forget-secret, and retried after a five-minute backoff if the helper is unavailable.
Completed groups queue the secret for deletion after the status is durably saved, subject to remaining references.
A new retry secret is saved in extension state before the superseded ID is queued for cleanup.
Removing a waiting/failed group schedules its secret for cleanup while preserving downloaded files.
Documentation says failed groups retain encrypted passwords for explicit retry, and uninstall retains residual encrypted state rather than deleting user data.
Tests cover cancel cleanup, completed-secret deletion, durable pending deletion, and retry after helper recovery.

verification.snapshotCodeReview: verified completion, superseded-retry, cancellation, and deferred-delete paths
verification.tests: Parent reports 113 TypeScript tests passing; focused assertions are present in the frozen test source. The reviewer did not rerun them.
verification.fixedPortion: Successful extraction, replaced retry secrets, and removed waiting/failed groups are eligible for cleanup; temporary helper failure preserves deletion intent without storing passwords in the pending-delete list.
verification.remainingRisk: A failed group that the user leaves in place retains its current encrypted password without an expiry. Uninstall also leaves such residual secret files. DPAPI remains at-rest protection, not a same-user isolation boundary.

findings.recommendation: Either accept and clearly document indefinite retry retention, or add an explicit cleanup/expiry control for failed groups and residual secrets during uninstall. Do not remove a failed group's secret before its retry state is intentionally discarded.

findings.summary: Installer now snapshots owned manifest/config and the prior registration, stages writes, commits registration last, and restores prior state on caught failure.

evidence.detail: Installer validates ownership and refuses malformed or foreign manifest/config content.
The transaction backs up existing files and registry snapshot, stages new files, replaces files, and commits the registration last.
Caught failures roll back registration/files; incomplete rollback retains and reports the backup directory.
Fault-injection test checks restoration of old files/mock registration and cleanup of partial files on failed first install without using the real registry.

verification.tests: Parent-reported parser and fault-injection smoke pass in artifacts/extraction-native/security-fixes.json; no production installer or registry was used or rerun by this reviewer.
verification.remaining: Rollback handles caught script failures; abrupt process termination or power loss cannot execute the catch path and may leave the timestamped backup directory for manual recovery.

findings.recommendation: No remaining issue for ordinary install/commit failures. If crash-consistency is a release requirement, add startup recovery or a single recoverable commit marker for abandoned .install-backup-* transactions.
